title: Career Roadmap: Policy Assistant
summary: A Policy Assistant supports the development, analysis, and evaluation of public policies, government programmes, and social or economic initiatives. The role combines economic reasoning, research, data analysis, report writing, and an understanding of how policy decisions affect people and communities.

blocks.text: For a student pursuing Economics (Hons) or Econometrics, this is a useful entry route into public policy research, development organisations, think tanks, government projects, and policy consulting.
Recommended degree
B.Sc. Economics (Hons), Econometrics, Economics, Statistics, or another relevant social science degree with quantitative coursework.
Core focus
Economic analysis, public policy, research methods, statistics, programme evaluation, and policy communication.
Potential workplaces
Public policy think tanks, research institutes, NGOs, development organisations, consulting firms, universities, and government-funded research projects.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Research policy issues using reports, academic studies, government publications, and public datasets.
Summarise policy proposals, laws, schemes, and economic developments.
Collect, clean, and analyse socioeconomic data.
Prepare policy briefs, background notes, presentations, and research summaries.
Track government programmes and policy developments.
Support surveys, stakeholder interviews, and field research.
Assist with monitoring and evaluating the outcomes of public programmes.
Help senior researchers assess the costs, benefits, and potential impacts of policy alternatives.

blocks.text: The exact responsibilities depend on whether the role focuses on research, government programme implementation, advocacy, or consulting.

This roadmap assumes a three-year B.Sc. programme. If the university offers a four-year honours or research pathway, use the additional year for a dissertation, advanced econometrics, or a research internship.
Year 1 — Economics and research foundations
Foundation

items.text: Study microeconomics, macroeconomics, mathematics, and introductory statistics.
Understand public goods, taxation, inflation, unemployment, and economic growth.
Read government budgets, economic surveys, and public policy news.
Practise academic writing, referencing, and Excel fundamentals.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Explain a public policy issue using reliable sources and basic economic concepts.
Year 2 — Quantitative analysis and policy research
Technical development

items.text: Learn econometrics, regression, research methodology, and data interpretation.
Practise R or Python and develop intermediate Excel skills.
Explore public finance, development economics, and labour economics.
Learn survey design, sampling, literature reviews, and evidence assessment.
Write short policy notes based on public datasets.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Produce a small, evidence-based analysis of a socioeconomic problem.
Year 3 — Applied policy research and career preparation
Career readiness

items.text: Study programme evaluation, cost-benefit analysis, and policy implementation.
Learn to interpret government statistics and assess data limitations.
Complete a policy research project with practical recommendations.
Seek internships with think tanks, NGOs, research centres, or development programmes.
Build a portfolio of policy briefs, data analysis, and presentations.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Apply for Policy Assistant, Research Assistant, Programme Research Intern, or Junior Policy Analyst roles.

rows.text: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, development economics, public finance

blocks.text: Build projects that show you can turn evidence into clear, useful policy recommendations.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Youth employment policy brief
Analyse publicly available employment indicators, identify a specific challenge, and compare possible policy interventions.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: a two-page policy brief, data charts, source list, and limitations.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Education programme analysis
Examine public indicators such as enrolment, attendance, or school completion across regions and investigate possible differences.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: cleaned dataset, comparison charts, research questions, and policy implications.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Public budget analysis
Compare allocations and reported expenditure for a selected sector, such as health, education, or rural development.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Excel analysis, budget visualisations, a short findings report, and data citations.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Econometric study of a social issue
Use a public dataset to investigate an association between factors such as education and earnings. Explain the method, assumptions, and limits of causal interpretation.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: R/Python notebook, regression tables, visualisations, and a research summary.
Use reliable public datasets and distinguish clearly between correlation and causation. A student analysis can inform discussion, but should not be presented as definitive proof that a policy works.

blocks.text: Useful additional learning areas include econometrics, research methodology, public finance, impact evaluation, and data visualisation. Prioritise demonstrable research skills over collecting unrelated certificates.
After your B.Sc., consider these routes depending on your intended specialisation:

blocks.label: M.A./M.Sc. Economics
blocks.text: Advanced economic theory, econometrics, and economic policy.

blocks.label: Master of Public Policy (MPP)
blocks.text: Policy design, implementation, evaluation, and governance.

blocks.label: Master of Public Administration (MPA)
blocks.text: Public management, institutions, and administration.

blocks.label: M.Sc. Econometrics / Applied Economics
blocks.text: Quantitative policy analysis and economic modelling.

blocks.label: Development Studies
blocks.text: Poverty, inequality, social protection, and development programmes.

blocks.label: Statistics / Data Science
blocks.text: A quantitative route into policy analytics, subject to admission requirements.
A postgraduate degree can expand access to research-oriented roles, although some assistant and internship positions accept undergraduates.

blocks.label: Stage 1
blocks.text: Research or Policy Intern
Support literature reviews, data collection, and background research.

blocks.label: Stage 2
blocks.text: Policy Assistant / Research Assistant
Prepare policy briefs, analyse data, and support research projects.

blocks.label: Stage 3
blocks.text: Policy Analyst / Research Associate
Lead analytical workstreams, evaluate programmes, and develop policy recommendations.

blocks.label: Stage 4
blocks.text: Senior Policy Researcher / Policy Advisor
Guide research agendas, advise decision-makers, and lead policy programmes.
Progression depends on research quality, experience, subject expertise, and the qualifications required by the employer.

Recommended target profile
By graduation, aim to have:

items.text: A solid foundation in economics, statistics, and econometrics.
Practical proficiency in Excel and R or Python.
Two to four policy research projects supported by credible data.
Strong policy writing and presentation skills.
At least one internship, research collaboration, or substantial independent project.

blocks.label: Best initial target
blocks.text: Policy Assistant or Research Assistant, with a longer-term path toward Policy Analyst or Research Associate. For quantitative policy roles, combine economic understanding with strong data analysis; for governance and programme roles, add field research, stakeholder engagement, and policy implementation experience.
